key_insight: SpecGP is a transformer-based model that produces energy-adaptable predictions of N‑glycopeptide structural spectra with enhanced fragment ion coverage, enabling better isomer discrimination and higher identification confidence via rescoring.
problem_solved: Predicting glycopeptide fragmentation spectra across varying collision energies and distinguishing structural isomers — a major bottleneck limiting accurate identification and structural characterization in glycoproteomics.
method: Transformer-based model that conditions spectral predictions on peptide/glycan structure and collision energy to produce energy-adaptable spectra.
Enhanced modelling of fragment ion coverage to capture isomer-specific spectral features for N‑glycopeptides.
Integration of predicted spectra into a rescoring pipeline to improve identification confidence and isomer discrimination.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for ML practitioners to build energy-aware spectral predictors and to incorporate model-based rescoring into proteomics pipelines, improving identification accuracy and enabling more reliable structural analysis.
visual_elements: Schematic: transformer input (peptide + glycan + collision energy) → predicted spectrum output
Overlay plots/heatmaps comparing predicted vs. experimental spectra across multiple collision energies
Before/after bar chart showing identification confidence and isomer discrimination improvement after rescoring
Pipeline diagram: raw data → SpecGP prediction → rescoring → validated identifications
paper_title: SpecGP as a transformer-based model for predicting energy-adaptable structural spectra of glycopeptides
paper_authors: Xianyong Wang, Rui Song, Zhuangzhuang Feng, Shisheng Sun
